chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast the Day of Arafah since the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed.

key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: Day of Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad fast on the Day of Arafah after Ramadan was revealed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) ceased fasting on the Day of Arafah once the obligatory fast of Ramadan was revealed, establishing the principle that the general obligation superseded the specific pre-Ramadan practice. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that fasting on Arafah is recommended (mustahabb) for those not performing Hajj, as the Prophet’s cessation was due to the new general command rather than abrogation of the virtue itself. This highlights the dynamic nature of fiqh where specific practices are integrated into the broader framework of Ramadan obligations.
